body.target_estimand: \(\tau_P(0)=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=0]\), interpreted as the unique continuous version
body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_n(0)=\operatorname{clip}_{[-3/4,3/4]}\{v(0)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Q_n^{-1}\widetilde R_n\}\) on the nonsingular branch, with \(R_n\asymp\rho_n=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\)

sampling_model.design: The known law \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\) has exact full support.
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from one law \(P\in\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L\) and the uniform design law, but not \(g_P,\mu_{0,P},\tau_P\); it uses deterministic localization and a finite projection correction rather than oracle nuisance inputs.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give the nuisance-elbow pointwise CATE rate and a localized higher-order R-learner, while Appendix B.8 matches the bounds on a known density whose local support is a union of separated cubes.
Theorem 2.1 bounds the affinity of two convex mixtures of product measures under a measurable partition and coordinate-local perturbations.
Theorems 3--5 establish matched local and global conditional-variance rates under random design using local U-statistics and coupled lower laws.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 give local-polynomial R-learner upper rates with deterministic smoothness-dependent tuning under known-density conditions.
The paper proves a quasi-oracle error bound for an R-learner under sufficient nuisance accuracy rather than a rough-nuisance pointwise minimax converse.

body.tldr: A smooth pointwise CATE can be statistically easier than its propensity and outcome regressions, but the known minimax converse below the nuisance elbow uses a covariate density with holes at bump transitions. This proposal fixes the covariate law to the exact known uniform distribution and asks whether the same pure-power rate survives. The proposed lower experiment uses smooth overlapping frames and correlated signs whose one-observation mixtures cancel exactly; conditioning on all covariates converts the shared-sign dependence into sparse geometric components, and a mixed-derivative affinity bound plus spanning-tree enumeration controls the full fixed-\(n\) mixture. Paired with a total finite projection estimator, the result would prove \(R_n\asymp n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\) with no logarithmic factor and show that oracle pointwise precision is unattainable throughout the strict below-elbow regime.

project_justification.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE supplies the candidate below-elbow rate and higher-order estimator, but its displayed hard laws remove covariate mass from nuisance-bump transition regions. A lower bound over that larger density model does not imply the same bound after fixing the design to exact uniformity, and the partition-local theorem of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax does not apply verbatim to overlapping smooth frames.
project_justification.niche: Exact known uniform design is simultaneously the cleanest upper-bound setting and the setting in which the published support-deletion cancellation is illegal. The unresolved object is therefore a same-class fixed-\(n\) product-mixture converse, rather than a new upper exponent or another oracle inequality.
project_justification.fill: The paper develops a correlated-sign smooth-frame prior and conditions on the observed covariates to factor its likelihood over sparse overlap components. A uniform component Hellinger inequality and random-geometric spanning-tree sum yield the missing nuisance-rate lower bound, while an explicit clipped projection U-statistic supplies the matching total upper bound.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE is the closest comparator: its Theorems 1--2 derive the same candidate exponent and higher-order local-polynomial architecture, while its lower proof and Appendix B.8 use a density supported on separated flat-top cells; Theorem 2 here asks whether that nuisance-dominated rate persists in the distinct singleton exact-uniform boundary experiment. RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax provides the two-mixture affinity theorem, but its first proof step is a deterministic partition with coordinate-local perturbations, whereas the present shared frames require factorization by random overlap components. ShenGaoWittenHan2020Variance supplies the closest random-design nonlinear-functional analogy: its conditional-variance lower proof controls repeated occupancy in local cells, motivating the treatment of non-singleton sign components. Kennedy2023DRCATE and NieWager2021RLearner explain why CATE estimation can approach an oracle regression problem under sufficient nuisance accuracy; they do not establish necessity on the rough exact-uniform class. RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2008HOIF motivates the finite projection and quadratic U-statistic correction. WagerAthey2018CausalForests is an application-facing consumer rather than a rate comparator: the theorem is a benchmark for \(\texttt{causal\_forest}\) and R-learner workflows, not a claim that an existing forest attains the bound.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The smooth-frame normalization, all-order H\"older bounds, uniform component derivative envelope, and inherited projection-risk calculation must each be checked independently. Exact singleton cancellation is insufficient by itself; any shared-sign term that survives outside non-singleton graph components, or any component constant growing faster than the sparse graph sum absorbs, kills the proposed converse.
body.honest_scope: The novelty-bearing claim is the full-support fixed-\(n\) lower bound. The upper exponent and nuisance elbow are inherited from the KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE architecture and are included to close the exact class with a total estimator. The proposal does not treat unknown design density, \(\kappa>0\) local overlap, adaptive tuning, confidence intervals, integrated loss, or performance of existing causal forests. As a sanity reduction, at \(S=S_{\star}\) the proposed exponent equals the classical oracle exponent \(\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\) without a logarithm.
